text.p: These are the main stories in Latvian newspapers on Thursday. Prepared for Reuters by the Co-operation Fund. Reuters has not verified these reports and does not vouch for their accuracy:
- Parliament is expected to approve the cabinet of Guntars Krasts as the new government commands 67 seats in the 100-seat parliament.

- St Petersburg starts a war against Baltic banks: the Russian federal revenue service has frozen the correspondent accounts of Latvian, Estonian and Lithuanian banks in the city, saying they have failed to pay tax.

- The Supreme Court threw out a case against Alexei Vidavski, the controversial mayor of Latvia's second city Daugavpils. Under the law he was banned from standing for office as he was a Communist Party member after January 13, 1991, the night of the Soviet crackdown in Vilnius. The prosecutor's office said it may launch another action against him.
- Finance Minister Robert Zile fears that the parties in the new government may dump the principle of a deficit-free budget, which he said would force him to resign.
- Energy prices are expected to rise again this year.
- President Guntis Ulmanis caused smiles when he mispronounced the word lawyer as liar during a presentation in San Francisco.
- Janis Naglis, the head of the privatisation agency, said the sale of state firms will be ended by next year.
- Police arrested a man who for several years has been opening graves and taking golden crowns and jewellery from the dead.
